DhSettings.name: Name

forceDiceLook.name: Dice look for the table
forceDiceLook.hint: With either Everyone choice, players and Assistant GMs roll in one full Gamemaster's Dice So Nice look, fixed the first time the game runs with it on. Everyone: Daggerheart gives Hope, Despair, advantage, and disadvantage dice Daggerheart's colors.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player's roll is whispered to that player and the GMs, and a GM's roll to the GMs. Only a GM's game.drpg.publicRoll macro is seen by everyone.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Another player's sheet shows only their name, portrait, Ultimate, Health, what they hold, and how many Experiences they have. Each player's own sheet stays whole.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search Tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: Search Tokens per room each time of day, 0 to 10. A Search uses one; a room with none left cannot be searched.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot change the dice, statistic, advantage, Experiences, or bonus in the roll window; those come from the action, a Hope Call, or the GM. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides characters in other rooms from players, even ones they could see through gaps in the walls. GMs see everything.

isoTokenShield.name: Guard token editing from Isometric Perspective
isoTokenShield.hint: Keeps Isometric Perspective out of the token configuration window, where it breaks editing. Turn this off to reach its Isometric tab.

regionFog.name: Rooms decide what players can see
regionFog.hint: A player sees their own room clearly and rooms they have visited dimly; the rest is fogged.

lockPlayerResources.name: Lock players' resources on the sheet
lockPlayerResources.hint: A player's own edit of their Actions, Hope, Health, Sanity, or statistics is put back or flagged to the GMs; with this off, it is only listed. Items and effects are checked either way. GMs are unaffected.

autoApproveTraits.name: Players' statistics need no approval
autoApproveTraits.hint: A player's statistic for a Search or a project goes through without your approval. A Resolve never asks for one.

friskForce.name: Frisk: forcing after a refusal
friskForce.hint: When off, an open Frisk only asks: a refusal or no answer ends it.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. The first crossing each time of day uses the Free Move; later ones cost an action or a Sprint crossing. Off, you handle movement yourself.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. Assign each student a Monokuma in the GM panel's Despair Flow.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's shared Fear bar. Each Monokuma keeps a Despair pool of their own either way. Turn it off to show the bar again.

enforceIsoWelcome.name: Keep Isometric Perspective's welcome window closed for everyone
enforceIsoWelcome.hint: Isometric Perspective's welcome window opens for nobody, the GM included.

enforceDhWelcome.name: Keep Daggerheart's welcome journal closed for everyone
enforceDhWelcome.hint: Daggerheart's welcome journal opens for nobody, the GM included.

enforcePlayerFiles.name: Keep players out of the file browser
enforcePlayerFiles.hint: Players cannot browse or upload files, and a click on a portrait opens nothing. Pictures already in the world still show.

liveKitInFoundry.name: Voice inside the Foundry window for everyone
liveKitInFoundry.hint: Voice runs in the Foundry window, with no separate tab.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Monokuma Legacy only: Press Start 2P on the HUD, tabs, names, and labels. Long text keeps the normal font. Only affects this browser.

wideProjectWindows.name: Wide project windows
wideProjectWindows.hint: Project windows open wider. Only affects this browser.

language.name: Language
language.hint: The language of this module's windows, cards, and sheet; Foundry keeps its own. Game names such as Truth Bullet stay in English. Needs a reload. Only affects this browser.

documentLanguage.name: Document language
documentLanguage.hint: The language of the documents the module writes into this world, one for everyone. Windows, cards, and the sheet follow each browser's Language. The first time the primary GM starts this world, it takes their language.

moveAudit.name: When a player's token moves through a wall
moveAudit.hint: Choose what happens when someone moves a player's token through a wall.
moveAudit.log: Note it in the Debug log

foundryToolWindows.name: The module's windows for Foundry's sidebar and scene controls
foundryToolWindows.hint: Puts a GM's Foundry sidebar and map tools in two windows, Foundry tools and Map tools, opened from the button in the corner. Players' screens stay the same. Saving reloads every screen once you confirm.

theme.name: Theme
theme.hint: How the module looks. Only affects this browser.

glassPulse.name: Glass pulse
glassPulse.hint: The slow darkening that travels around the frame. Turn it off to keep the glass and stop it breathing. Only affects this browser.

highContrast.name: High contrast
highContrast.hint: Brighter fine print, solid hairlines, and opaque panels with no blur behind them. If your system asks for more contrast, you get this look even with the setting off. Only affects this browser.

sequences.name: Full-screen sequences
sequences.hint: Plays the Class Trial's entry, the verdict, the clock's turns and flashes, and the day boards full screen for everyone. When off, only the trial's and the verdict's sounds play. Esc skips one.

reducedMotion.name: Reduced motion
reducedMotion.hint: Hold the interface still on this browser, whatever the operating system says. This client only.

hudTicker.name: State name behind the clock
hudTicker.hint: The time of day, faint, behind the clock. Only affects this browser.

bulletSort.name: How Truth Bullets are grouped
bulletSort.hint: Sorts your Truth Bullets by chapter, the default, or by room. The switch is in your inventory, beside them. Only affects this browser.

glassBlur.name: Glass blurs the map
glassBlur.hint: The glass frosts the map behind it. If the game stutters, turn this off first. Only affects this browser.

messengerSound.name: Messenger sounds
messengerSound.hint: Plays the messenger's sounds for a message sent, a message received, and a question for the GM. Only affects this browser.

uiScale.name: Interface scale
uiScale.hint: Sets the size of the module's windows and text, and with them Foundry's windows and the sheet, from 80% to 140%. The map keeps its size. Only affects this browser.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. Only affects this browser.

musicEnabled.name: Music follows the game state
musicEnabled.hint: Changes the playlist with the game: an Eclipse, a trial, an investigation, the time of day, a pause. Assign the playlists first in the Sound window.

voiceEnabled.name: Separate voice in each room
voiceEnabled.hint: You hear only the people in your room. Needs LiveKit AVClient.

voiceTile.name: Voice tile instead of the camera dock
voiceTile.hint: Hides the cameras. The tile shows how many people are in your channel.

SettingsWindow.title: DRPG Settings

why.noScene: the scene it was on no longer exists. The student can propose it again on another scene.
why.twoRooms: the stretch does not join two rooms. Pick a stretch on a wall between two rooms.
why.gmOnly: only a GM can do this. Try it again as a GM.
why.noStore: the GMs' record of this season's passages is not loaded. Reload the world, then take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.noBuilder: its builder is no longer a student of this world. Make a new project for another student if it should still happen.
why.idTaken: another passage took its place at the same moment. Take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.breached: that wall already has a breach. Close that breach first, or pick another wall.
why.wholeWall: the stretch takes the whole wall, and nothing of it would stand. Pick a shorter stretch.
why.noBreach: that breach is no longer there: a GM or another project closed it first. Nothing is left to do.
why.wallGone: the wall it was cut from is gone. The room beyond has its lock and its bedroom key back; delete the hole by hand with the walls tool.
why.cannotClose: the passage could not be closed. Close it by hand in the Passages tab.
why.notKnown: the character does not know that passage, or it is closed already. Check it in the Passages tab.
why.isBreach: that is a breach. To give its wall back, use Close the breach on the Passages tab, or a Close the breach project.
why.noSide: it has no side in the room where the character stands. Approve it only from a room the passage or the breach opens into.
why.lockWhole: that lock is not broken, so there is nothing to repair.
why.lockTaken: a project repairs that lock already.
why.lockFar: that lock is on no door of the room where the character stands. Approve it only from that room or one next to it.
why.noWall: the wall is gone. Pick the stretch again.
why.taken: the stretch overlaps another passage on that wall. Pick a stretch beside it.
why.levels: a room beside the stretch is on another floor. Pick a stretch on the character's floor.
why.notBetween: the stretch does not stand between two rooms. Pick a stretch of a wall between two rooms.
why.otherRooms: the stretch's two ends stand between different rooms. Pick both ends between the same two rooms.
why.short: the stretch is too short. Pick a longer stretch.
why.door: that wall is a door. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.noMove: that wall does not stop anyone. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.sameEnds: the stretch needs two different ends. Pick it again.
why.offWall: the stretch is no longer on that wall. Pick it again.
why.floor: that wall is not on the character's floor. Pick a wall of that floor.
why.notOwn: the item is not on the builder's own sheet: it was given away or taken, or it is on a shared sheet. Only an item on the builder's own sheet can be repaired.
why.notRepairable: the item is not a Usable or a piece of Gear, or it is neither broken nor worn. There is nothing to repair.
why.nothingBack: there is nothing to put back. Cut the breach again by hand if it should stand.
why.itemBack: the item's state before the repair was not recorded, or the item is gone, so nothing changed.
why.brokenSince: the item was broken or worn again since, and is left as it is.
why.repairTooSmall: the item's tier went up since this repair was approved, so nothing was mended. Approve a new repair of the right size.
why.unknown: the module could not say why; the reason is in the GM's console.

cannotAfford.other: You have {left} actions left and this needs {needed}.

tokensLeft.other: {room} has {n} Search Tokens left this time of day.

Action.dynamicPlaceholder: e.g. I water the plants in the garden, looking for anything buried.

Action.noRoomNote: Your token is outside every room.
Action.callsGmNote: The GM judges this one. Your roll and your request go to them.

placeholder.analyze: e.g. Analyzing the torn cloth from the hallway.
placeholder.directMurder: Who, where, and how - as agreed beforehand.

murderWitness.other: You are not alone with your victim - {n} other people would see it. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.

Action.sabotageWatched: {actor} is doing something to {project} in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.

Action.situationAfterRoll: {n} from the situation: the total that counts is {total}.

Action.murderPromptParked: What are you doing, and how? The GM reads this when the lights come up.

Action.murderParkedToast: Declared. The answer comes when the Eclipse does.
Action.murderSecondDeclaration: {killer} also declared a direct murder in the dark, but an incident was already open. Their attempt was refused and their action is spent.
Action.murderCancelled: {killer}'s direct murder came to nothing in {room} - {reason}
Action.murderOpens: {killer} declared a direct murder during the Eclipse and ended it alone with {victim} in {room}. The incident is open.
Action.noVariants: Nothing here can be done right now.
Action.requestOptional: Optional - leave it empty and the GM rules on the roll alone.
Action.murderNeedsApproval: A direct murder, declared in the dark. Nothing opens until you allow it - and who they end up alone with is not settled yet.
Action.murderRefused: The GM did not allow it. The action is spent.
Action.murderApprovedGm: {name}'s direct murder is allowed. It resolves when the Eclipse ends.
Action.murderRefusedGm: {name}'s direct murder is refused. Their action is spent.

Action.murderAsk: {killer} declared a direct murder in the dark and has ended up alone with {victim} in {room}. Open the incident?
Action.murderAskNote: You were asked this when it was declared and it is still unanswered. Refusing opens nothing; the action stays spent either way.
Action.dynamicMissedGm: The roll missed. There is nothing to give; the action stays spent.

Analyze.noBullets: You have nothing left to analyze.
Analyze.sent: The result for {name} is on a card of its own.
Analyze.failed: You cannot make sense of {name}. It stays with you, still Neutral, and you cannot try this one again until the next chapter.
Analyze.failedShown: You cannot make sense of {name}. It stays with you as it is, and you cannot try this one again until the next chapter.
Analyze.critPrompt: {actor} identified {name} as {a} {type} on a critical, which earns them a substantial hint as well. Write the hint and send it with Reply.

analyseBulletHint.other: Roll Head to learn what one of your {n} Truth Bullets really is; a miss locks it until the chapter ends.

Analyze.askHintHint: Ask the GM where to look; a higher total gets a clearer hint.
Analyze.findStashHint: Look for another student's stash here; {n}+ or a critical finds a new one and whose it is.
Analyze.stashNothing: You go over the room and find nothing anybody has tried to hide.

Analyze.passageNothing: You find no hidden passage here.
Analyze.passageFound: There is a secret passage in this room, to {to}. You know it now: your map shows it, and while it is open, you can go through it.

Analyze.stashFoundGm: {finder} rolled {total} and found {who}'s hidden stash in {room}. {who} has not been told.
Analyze.stashSent: You go over the room looking for anything that does not belong.

Items.itemNoEffect: Works, no effect: use it up
Items.creativeRefused: The GM ruled that “{item}” does nothing here. It stays with you.

Items.caption: Give / take
Items.name: Name

Items.overCapNote: You can give past the limit, and you then get a warning that the student is over it.
Items.lost: “{item}” is no longer in your inventory.
Items.failed: That did not work. See the console.
Items.useTier0Tooltip: Tier 0: tell the GM what you do with it.

Items.noneReadied: You are holding nothing ready. Only what is in your hand counts in a project, a sabotage, a clean-up, or an incident.

Items.carriesNothing: {actor} is carrying nothing and has nothing stashed.

Monocub.cannotMeddle: Not enough action, or not enough Hope.
Monocub.mustBeDead: Only a character who has already died becomes a Monocub.
Monocub.onlyTwoActions: A Monocub moves freely and uses its own tiles: Confusion, Tinker, Redeem, Ask for Hope and Ghost Bet.
Monocub.opted: {name} has joined the GMs as a Monocub.
Monocub.dialogIntro: After their own Class Trial, a dead player can join as a Monocub.
Monocub.giveHope: Turn a Monokuma's Despair into Hope
Monocub.giveAtLeast: Type how much Despair to turn into Hope - at least {n}.
Monocub.silencedNote: Ticked by itself when this Monocub is in the room of a murder. Tick it if they saw the crime some other way. They can't discuss it until the chapter ends; Confusion still works.
Monocub.needHope: Confusion costs Hope and you have none. Ask a GM to convert some Despair.
Monocub.nobodyHere: Nobody in this room to use Confusion on.
Monocub.meddleIntro: Nudge somebody's next roll from the sidelines. Everyone in your room sees you roll, so they may work out it was you.
Monocub.tiersIntro: The GM throws the dice. What the total does:
Monocub.grantBonus: +1 with Help, -1 with Hinder, on their next roll
Monocub.grantAdvantage: advantage with Help, disadvantage with Hinder, on their next roll
Monocub.tinkerIntro: Push a project in your room one step forward or back, if someone worked on it this time of day. Your room sees you roll and which way, not on what.
Monocub.tinkerRefused: Tinker doesn't reach it. You keep your action and Hope.
Monocub.noProjectHere: No project in this room to use Tinker on.
Monocub.grantStep: the project one step forward with Help, back with Hinder
Monocub.tinkerHeld: Tinker: {name} holds one step short of done. Somebody living has to finish it.
Monocub.bribeAsk: {name} offers {cub} {cost} Hope for a favour you agree on. Accept, and it goes into your purse.
Monocub.bribeOffered: You offer {name} a Bribe of {cost} Hope. You pay only if they accept.
Monocub.bribeOfferedCub: {name} offers you a Bribe of {cost} Hope.
Monocub.bribeRefused: {name} turns down your Bribe. You keep your Hope.
Monocub.bribeAcceptedCub: You accept {name}'s Bribe: {cost} Hope in your purse.
Monocub.bribeUnpaid: Your Bribe to {name} could not be paid and is closed. You keep your Hope.
Monocub.bribeUnpaidCub: {name}'s Bribe could not be paid and is closed.
Monocub.bribeLapsed: Your Bribe to {name} went unanswered and lapsed. You keep your Hope.
Monocub.bountyPosted: A Bounty: {reward} Hope to the first Monocub whose Confusion hinders {name}.

bountyOwedCancelled.other: The {n} Despair {pool} owed for it is cancelled.

bountyDespairBack.other: The {n} Despair {pool} paid for it is back in the pool.

Monocub.bountyPaid: You claim the Bounty on {name}: {n} Hope in your purse.
Monocub.bountyNoDespair: Your pool has not the Despair for a Bounty.

Monocub.betOwnCase: No Ghost Bet while your own case is open.
Monocub.betWitness: No Ghost Bet for a witness of the crime.

Monocub.panelOffer: {name} offers you a Bribe of {cost} Hope.

flag.third: A third Bribe this chapter between {name} and {cub}.

Monocub.critHelpNothing: The player had every action left: there was none to give back.
Monocub.critHelpNothingTarget: A moment's luck, but no action of yours was spent: nothing comes back.
Monocub.critHinderNothing: The player had no action left to waste.
Monocub.critHinderNothingTarget: A moment's confusion, but you had no action left to lose.
Monocub.meddleRefused: Confusion doesn't reach them. You keep your action and Hope.
Monocub.wrongVerdictCard: The one who did it walks free. Until the next trial, don't use your moves for or against that person, their projects, Bribes or Ghost Bets.
Monocub.wrongVerdictTold: Told the verdict let the killer go: {names}.
Monocub.inviteIntro: The GMs invite {name} back as a Monocub: you keep playing from the sidelines, with Confusion, Tinker, Redeem and Ask for Hope.

Monocub.invited: {name} is invited. They become a Monocub once their player accepts the Monocub Rule.
Monocub.redeemUsed: You've used Redeem today. It comes back tomorrow.
Monocub.darkened: The darkening blocks Hope this time of day.
Monocub.askStillOpen: Your Ask for Hope is still waiting for a GM.
Monocub.moveRefused: That move doesn't go through now. You keep your action and Hope.
Monocub.askNotNowTold: Your Ask for Hope: not now. You can ask again.
Monocub.silencedNoteShort: You stumbled onto the crime. No discussing it until next chapter.
Monocub.noneYet: Nobody has opted in as a Monocub yet.
Monocub.silenceOn: You're a witness: you can't discuss the crime until this chapter ends.

Mastermind.finalRunningNote: This trial is the Final Trial.

Mastermind.noneSet: No Mastermind set. Pick one from the GM panel first.

straw.openedBare: Students stand in Zone A for {a} or in Zone B for {b}. The count comes in {seconds} s.

Floor.nobodyForTrial: There is nobody alive to hold a Class Trial with.
Floor.newTrialConfirm: This chapter already has a verdict. Open a new trial? A second verdict means another execution and another round of Level Ups.
Floor.newTrialRefused: This chapter already has a verdict, so the Class Trial was not opened again. A second trial opens from Start the Class Trial, which asks first.
Floor.eclipseFirst: An Eclipse is running, so nothing was opened. End the Eclipse first.
Floor.nowMovedOn: The turn had already moved on, so Skip changed nothing. Press it again if this turn should still end.

Floor.registerEmpty: The Blackened register is empty, and a student died this chapter. Was the incident closed? A killer goes on the register when their incident closes.
Floor.startTrialIntro: A Class Trial opens in discussion: everybody talks, and evidence goes on the table without taking the floor. The Nonstop Debate is something you open inside it.
Floor.startTrialStepPhase: The campaign moves to Class Trial.
Floor.startTrialStepAnnounce: The trial is announced in chat and the music follows.

trialBudget.one: {n} student has this time of day's actions for the trial.
trialBudget.other: {n} students have this time of day's actions for the trial.

Floor.trialOpened: The Class Trial is in session. Talk it through; the debate opens when the GM says so.
Floor.endTrialConfirm: This closes the debate, ends the Class Trial and returns the campaign to Daily Life.
Floor.endTrialNotChapter: The chapter is not ended - use End the chapter for the reveal and the next chapter.
Floor.endTrialExecutes: Ending the trial carries out the sentence: {names}.

lead.openAgain: The GM overruled an Objection after its exchange, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the time it had left, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.reopen: The exchange has closed the debate, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the same question and budget, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.closeDebate: The debate is open. Close it when the room has argued it out, then send the ballots from The vote.
lead.now: An objection or a rebuttal holds the floor. It runs out on its own; Skip on the bar cuts it short.
lead.vote: The ballots are out. When they are back, Close and count in The vote.
lead.verdict: The vote is counted. Deliver the verdict, then end the chapter.
lead.finishVerdict: The verdict stopped before every step was done. Finish the verdict, then end the chapter.
lead.finishElsewhere: The verdict stopped before every step was done. Only {name} can finish it, so that each of its steps is done once: ask {name}, then end the chapter.
lead.verdictElsewhere: {name} is giving the verdict. If their browser was reloaded inside it, Finish the verdict is on their console; end the chapter once the verdict is done.
lead.chapterEnd: The verdict is in. End the chapter for the reveal and the next chapter.
lead.caseSummary: The verdict is in. Show the players the case summary, then end the chapter.
lead.sentenceWaits: The trial goes on: the sentence is carried out when it ends.

lead.zones: A zone mode holds the floor: everyone answers by where their token stands. Count now and Skip on the bar bring the count forward; End this mode ends it.
lead.scrum: The Straw Poll split the class. A Scrum Debate from Hall zones lets the two camps argue it out; the debate and the vote are still open to you.

Music.fadeNote: Set the fade length in each playlist's Fade Duration. When a body is found and nothing is mapped to it, the music goes silent, and a track you put on yourself stops too.
Music.noPlaylists: No playlists yet. Make them in the Playlists sidebar.

state.bodyFound: A body has been found (silence unless mapped)

Music.playNowNote: Plays a track from “{name}” on repeat. Stop it, and the music that was playing before comes back.
Music.wasReset: The track stopped, and the music it interrupted picks up where it left off.
Music.playFailed: That track would not play. See the console.
Music.situationalMade: “{name}” is ready. Add your scene tracks to it in the Playlists sidebar, and they appear here.
Music.makeFailed: The playlist could not be created. See the console.

diag.clock: Clock: phase={phase} time of day={time} eclipse={eclipse} paused={paused}
diag.cueMissing: missing, so the Play button has nothing to draw from
diag.onCue: {name}: the cue playlist, never played for a state
diag.noState: No state applies, so the music is left alone.
diag.unmapped: "{state}" is the active state but has no playlist to play, so the music is left alone. Map one: GM panel, Sound, Music.

Cleanup.title: Cleaning up
Cleanup.priceGone: Covering yourself took what this attempt was going to cost. Nothing else was spent.
Cleanup.keptSanity: The attempt keeps its price: the cover story was already told.
Cleanup.withTool: “{item}” (Tier {tier}) in hand - advantage, and that much off the threshold.
Cleanup.bareHands: You hold no tool, so you clean with bare hands, without advantage.
Cleanup.noneReadied: No Cleaning Tool readied. Hold one ready on the Inventory tab first.

blocked.noIncident: No incident is running, so there is nothing to clean up. Stage 6 opens when one ends.
blocked.notYet: The incident is still going on. Clean-up opens the moment it is over - as a Finishing Blow, or by the GM ending it.
blocked.notYours: You are not the one cleaning up this scene.
blocked.monokuma: Monokuma does not clean up after himself. A killing made as a point is meant to be found.

Cleanup.trailNobody: There is nobody left to frame.
Cleanup.moveHint: Spend {n} Sanity to carry the body out of this room; it always leaves an Evident Remnant.
Cleanup.bodyNotHere: The body is not in this room. You have to be standing over it to carry it anywhere.
Cleanup.nothingHere: Nothing to clean up in this room.
Cleanup.allReinforced: Every Remnant here is reinforced. None of it comes off.
Cleanup.rerollLost: A Reroll of a clean-up was not replayed: there was no record here of the attempt it takes back. Its first roll goes back on the card and the Hope is returned.
Cleanup.reinforced: The {what} will not come off. Whatever left it, left it for good.
Cleanup.vanished: The Remnant you were working on is already gone. The effort still cost you.
Cleanup.freeTonight: Your own scene, tonight: no action, {n} Sanity each.
Cleanup.leftTrace: Your cleaning left a Remnant of its own.

band.despair: Gone - but you were not careful about it.
band.failure: It will not come off, and you made a mess trying.

Cleanup.gmTool: Readied: “{item}” (Tier {tier}) - advantage, and {tier} off every threshold below.
Cleanup.gmNoTool: No Cleaning Tool readied - bare hands, no advantage.
Cleanup.gmNothingHere: No Remnants in the room the killer is standing in.

gmAttemptsLeft.one: Sanity left for {n} more attempt. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you end the murder - ending it destroys the Murder Weapon that was used; the cleaning tool goes when the body is found.
gmAttemptsLeft.other: Sanity left for {n} more attempts. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you end the murder - ending it destroys the Murder Weapon that was used; the cleaning tool goes when the body is found.

Cleanup.refundUnheld: {name}'s clean-up asked for {what} back, and the GMs' audit held no record here to check it was paid: nothing was given back. If it was paid, give it back by hand.
Cleanup.freeAttempt: This attempt costs no Sanity: the critical Finishing Blow paid for it.
Cleanup.trailPlanted: Planted a Prep Remnant ({visibility}) pointing at {name}.
Cleanup.authorsCopy: You know this Remnant: it is on your sheet.
Cleanup.bodyMoved: The body has been moved to {room}.
Cleanup.bodyStuck: The body would not move. It still lies where it fell, and no trail of dragging was left.
Cleanup.noBody: There is no body here to move.
Cleanup.bodyNote: {name}'s body was dragged out of here towards {room}.
Cleanup.seenCleaning: {actor} is doing something in {room}, and not hiding it well.
Cleanup.moveIntro: The body is in {room}. Choose where you are dragging it. Costs {n} Sanity.
Cleanup.moveAlwaysTrace: This always leaves an Evident trace behind, whatever the dice say. You cannot drag a corpse quietly. Bedrooms are not on the list: a body behind somebody's locked door names a suspect for you.
Cleanup.moveFar: Two rooms away - a critical only
Cleanup.moveFarNote: A room two away needs a critical. Any other hit carries the body only as far as the room between.
Cleanup.bodyShort: It got only as far as {room}: {far} needed a critical.
Cleanup.bodyNowhere: There is nowhere to take it - no room connects to this one, or the only ones that do are bedrooms.
Cleanup.toolsBroken: {items} is ruined. It is still in your inventory, and it is still evidence.
Cleanup.transformActionHint: Rename a non-Reinforced Remnant: a GM's approval makes it a Tamper Remnant, a refusal gives nothing back.
Cleanup.transformActionIntro: You are not removing this. You are making it read as something else. Write what the next person through the door will find.
Cleanup.reshapeTextPlaceholder: A tin went over during the afternoon. Nobody cleaned it up properly.
Cleanup.reshapeNeedsBoth: Write both a name and a description - an empty lie is not a lie. The window is open again with what you wrote.
Cleanup.reshapeNothingSaid: A reshape needs both a name and a description, and this one did not carry both, so the Remnant still reads exactly as it did.
Cleanup.reshapeVoided: Taken back by a Reroll or replaced by a later attempt before {name} ruled on it.
Cleanup.reshapeTakenBack: A Reroll or a later attempt took this one's place, so this card no longer rules on anything.
Cleanup.alreadyRuled: This reshape has already been ruled on - by {name}.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedErased: {name} kept your story off the Remnant. The critical still took it: the Remnant is gone.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTitle: A Remnant made to read differently
Cleanup.reshapeRulingQuieter: It rolled well enough to be one band harder to spot as well.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTies: They are the killer, so approving this also marks the Remnant as part of the murder.

reshapeRulingCopies.one: Approving leaves the {n} Truth Bullet already copied from it reading as it was found; whoever finds it afterwards reads the new words.
reshapeRulingCopies.other: Approving leaves the {n} Truth Bullets already copied from it reading as they were found; whoever finds it afterwards reads the new words.

Cleanup.reshapeWaiting: You worked it over into “{name}”. Until the GM says otherwise it still reads as it did.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclined: {name} ruled that the Remnant still says what it said. The turn and the Sanity are spent.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedGm: Declined. {name} was told the Remnant is unchanged.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingGone: That Remnant is no longer there, so there is nothing to relabel.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsent: A reshaped Remnant could not be delivered to a thread. Nothing of its story was written on the Remnant - rule on it in words, and relabel it by hand if you allow it. On the erase road the Remnant was erased, as the critical bought.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsentPlayer: You worked it over, but your story did not reach the GM. Say it out loud; nothing has been written on the Remnant.
Cleanup.reshaped: {from} now reads as “{name}”: {band} {kind}. Whoever finds it finds your story, not what was there.
Cleanup.transformActionNote: A GM approves your words first, and a refusal gives back nothing you paid. Approved, it becomes a Tamper Remnant, which admits that somebody handled it and lies about everything else. A critical also makes it one band quieter and hands back what you paid.
Cleanup.transformIntro: You have time to do more than wipe it. Erase the Remnant, or leave it saying something else entirely - and, this well rolled, choose how loudly it says it.
Cleanup.transformNote: Nobody sees you decide. Erasing happens now. Leaving something else waits for a GM's approval first: whoever finds it then finds your story, as a Tamper Remnant. If the GM refuses, the Remnant is erased all the same and nothing you paid comes back.

Reserve.fieldHealth: How much Health is left. Type a number to change it.
Reserve.fieldSanity: How much Sanity is left. Type a number to change it.

Murder.openingReask: Ask for the opening roll again
Murder.openingReaskSent: The invitation to throw the opening roll was sent again.
Murder.openingReaskWait: The invitation was sent a moment ago - give them a few seconds.
Murder.victimNoticedNext: The victim noticed. Nothing happens by itself now: they may use their Free Move, if they still have it, and the incident stays open until you end it from the tracker.
Murder.openIntro: An opening roll, then turns. Direct: the killer rolls; a trap: the victim.
Murder.indirect: A trap (the victim alone, losing double)
Murder.indirectCost: A trap is built as projects. Plan about {low}-{high} progress in total, roughly {fewest} to {actions}.
Murder.needOne: There must be at least one living student.
Murder.openSelfNote: One name in both seats: this opens as a death by their own hand. There is no Stage 5 - the opening roll decides whether they go through with it, and the incident goes straight to Stage 6.
Murder.killerNotAlive: {name} is named as the killer and is not among the living, so the Killer list shows somebody else. Pick who this murder is for.
Murder.roomsDiffer: {killer} is in {killerRoom}, {victim} in {victimRoom}. Bring them together, or open it anyway.
Murder.opened: {killer} is moving on {victim}. The opening roll has gone to {roller}.
Murder.openedSelf: {name} is moving on themselves. The opening roll has gone to them.
Murder.openedSelfNote: Stage 5 is skipped: there is no confrontation to run. If the roll lands, the incident goes straight to Stage 6 - the arrangements they make before dying. They stay alive until you close the incident.
Murder.selfWentThrough: You went through with it. There is no fight to have. Stage 6 is open on your sheet: whatever you leave the room as, you leave it as now.
Murder.resolutionNoteSelf: Stage 6, with nobody left to hide it from but the class. They can see and clean their own Remnants, and they are still alive to do it - closing the incident is what makes the death real.
Murder.trackerStateSelf: {stage} · no turns - Stage 5 does not run
Murder.afterSelf: By their own hand - nobody else was in the room, and the class has only the scene to go on.
Murder.afterIntroSelf: {name}, by their own hand. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.dayNote: Not night, so the opening roll is unmodified.

keyCount.one: This case will leave {n} Key Remnant.
keyCount.other: This case will leave {n} Key Remnants.

Murder.trackerCastGone: This incident names somebody the world does not have any more ({who}). Nothing can move it on - press End the murder.
Murder.ranOut: {name} is out of Health and out of Sanity. The incident ends and they are dead - no Finishing Blow was needed, and none was earned.
Murder.rerollLost: A Reroll of a crisis action was not replayed: there was no record of it here, or the incident closed or moved on first. Its first roll goes back on the card and the Hope is returned. If the incident closed while it was being taken back, check that action's Remnant and the sheets by hand.
Murder.passTooSoon: The turn was passed a moment ago. Press Pass the turn again to pass the next one.
Murder.nobodyElse: There is nobody else alive to walk in.
Murder.endConfirm: Stop tracking this murder? Lost Health and Sanity, items, and Remnants stay as they are.
Murder.afterTitle: The incident is over - what now
Murder.afterIntro: {killer} against {victim}. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.afterNoRoom: The victim's token is outside every room. Put it where the body is before announcing it.
Murder.afterAutopsy: The autopsy Truth Bullet has not been issued.
Murder.afterDirect: A direct murder - whoever was in the room saw it happen.
Murder.afterIndirect: A trap - nobody saw it, and setting it left Remnants of its own.
Murder.escapeIntro: {victim} and {third} walked out on {killer}. Nobody died, so there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue and no Class Trial to hold. The incident ends.
Murder.escapeRoom: It happened in {room}, and what the fight left behind is still there.
Murder.escapeNoRoom: No room is recorded for this incident, so place whatever it left behind by hand.
Murder.escapeWitness: {victim} and {third} both saw who it was. What they do with that is the table's business.
Murder.escapeKiller: {killer} is not Blackened. Nothing has changed for them except that two people know.
Murder.afterSurvived: {victim} survived the attack by {killer}. Nobody died, so there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue and no Class Trial to hold, and nobody is Blackened for it. What the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.afterInterrupted: The incident was interrupted before anything was decided - nobody died. There is no body, no autopsy and nobody Blackened for it; what the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.closedVictimYou: The incident is over. You can act again.
Murder.useItemGone: That is not on you any more - nothing to use.
Murder.useItemFumbled: It stays in your pocket, and somebody saw you reaching for it.
Murder.useItemAsked: The GM decides if it works. Until then the item is not used up.
Murder.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
Murder.actionHindered: They have made this harder - you roll at disadvantage.
Murder.noStressLeft: Resolution actions cost Sanity, and you have none.
Murder.nothingLeftToSpend: There is nothing left to spend. Sanity and Health are both gone.
Murder.advantageNext: Advantage on the next attempt at this action.
Murder.noKillerLeft: Every killer in this incident is dead. The victim acts alone from here, turn after turn, until the incident is closed.
Murder.killerChooses: Critical - the killer chooses where both points come off: Health or Sanity.

hinderedActions.one: Their opponent rolls {actions} at disadvantage for {turns} turn.
hinderedActions.other: Their opponent rolls {actions} at disadvantage for {turns} turns.

blockedActions.one: Their opponent cannot use {actions} for {turns} turn.
blockedActions.other: Their opponent cannot use {actions} for {turns} turns.

Murder.rolesSwapped: The roles are reversed. The killer is the one bleeding now.
Murder.victimDead: The victim is dead. The killer is Blackened.
Murder.resolutionNote: Stage 6. The killer now sees the Remnants on the map and can use resolution actions. Reinforced Remnants stay put. A Murder Weapon that was used is destroyed.
Murder.thirdIntro: One free choice: get them out with you, take a side, or turn away.
Murder.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
Murder.actionDenied: That action is not open to you now.
Murder.drainStopped: The bleeding stops - no further Health or Sanity is lost this incident.
Murder.indirectBegins: The trap closes. The incident begins with the victim alone, losing 2 a turn.
Murder.tierZeroIntro: {actor} is swinging {item}, a Tier 0 object. A Tier 0 item may count as Tier 1 or 2 when the killer is being creative - how good is this use?
Murder.tierZeroNote: Tier 0 deals 1 damage, Tier 1 deals 2, Tier 2 deals 2 and 3 on a critical. Dismissing this leaves it at Tier 0.
Murder.improvised: Snatched a weapon out of the struggle: “{item}” (Tier {tier}).
Murder.improvisedNote: Grabbed mid-incident. A Murder Weapon like any other.
Murder.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action - Survive, Escape Together, a Finishing Blow, or, if you only walked in on it, Averted Eyes.
Murder.oneAtATime: There is already an incident running. It has to finish before another can start.
Murder.crisisPrompt: What are you doing about it?
Murder.crisisBrief: One action a turn. A row that is shut says why.
Murder.nothingToDo: There is nothing left for you to do this round.
Murder.actionsLocked: You are in an incident. Everything you can do is behind {tile}; Hope Calls still work.
Murder.thirdJoined: {name} throws in with the killer and stays in the incident.
Murder.thirdLeft: {name} turns away and leaves. They take no part in this.
Murder.thirdEscapedAlone: {name} gets out alone. The victim stays where they are, and {name} takes no part in this any more.
Murder.openingYours: This roll is yours, and it is the only one. It cannot be skipped.
Murder.openingRequired: This roll cannot be skipped. Throw it.
Murder.openingDeclined: {name} did not throw the opening roll. Stage 4 cannot be skipped: ask again from the Incident tracker, or end the incident.
Murder.openingRemnantNote: {name} sensed the attempt ({band}). Something of the struggle was left to notice.

leftRemnants.one: Leaves a Remnant behind, and the killer cannot wipe it.
leftRemnants.other: Leaves {n} Remnants behind, and the killer cannot wipe them.

keyRemnantsStale.one: The roles reversed, so the case changed: the {n} Key Remnant was planned around a killer who is now the victim. Write {n} new one before the Investigation - the count came off the opening roll and has not changed.
keyRemnantsStale.other: The roles reversed, so the case changed: the {n} Key Remnants were planned around a killer who is now the victim. Write {n} new ones before the Investigation - the count came off the opening roll and has not changed.

Murder.nightNoteDirect: It is night: the killer's opening roll has advantage.
Murder.nightNoteIndirect: It is night: the victim's opening roll has disadvantage.
Murder.betrayalNote: {third} walked in on this and is still standing. They may turn on {killer} until the day ends. Outside an Eclipse it is the one killing in the game that needs no declaration in advance; in one it is declared, and opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalIntro: {third} kills {killer}. This closes as a second murder, with {third} as the killer and {killer} as the victim - a fresh incident from the opening roll, not a continuation of the one that just ended.
Murder.betrayalRule: Two bodies in one day, so the Class Trial has two killings to untangle. Whoever is Blackened for the first is not automatically Blackened for the second. You have until the end of the day to decide.
Murder.betrayalConfirmEclipse: An Eclipse is running, so the betrayal is declared now and opens when the Eclipse ends, like any action declared in one. It costs an action, and the action stays spent even if the betrayal cannot open then.
Murder.betrayalParked: Your betrayal is declared. It opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalAnnounce: A second incident opens on {killer} - the betrayal.
Murder.betrayalRefused: The betrayal could not open: {why}. It stays on offer until the day ends.

betrayalWhy.spent: it is no longer on offer
betrayalWhy.failed: the GM's client could not open it
betrayalWhy.trial: a Class Trial is in session
betrayalWhy.dead: one of the two is no longer alive

Murder.victimUnderAttackBy: {killer} is moving on you. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours. On your character sheet, under Actions, press Fight back.
Murder.victimSomeoneMoves: Someone is moving on you. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours. On your character sheet, under Actions, press Fight back.
Murder.victimTrapSprung: The trap closes. You did not see it in time. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours - on your character sheet, under Actions, press Fight back.
Murder.offTurn: It is their turn. Your crisis actions open when it comes back to you.
Murder.breakdownDisadvantage: You are in Breakdown, so this roll is at disadvantage until some Sanity comes back.
Murder.gmPicksTrait: Rolls: {traits} - you propose one below, the GM approves or changes it.
Murder.youPickTrait: Rolls: {traits} - Resolve is armed, so you pick one in the roll window.
Murder.criticalChoiceIntro: The blow lands exactly where you wanted it. Both points come off the same reserve - their body, or their nerve.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillers: {victim} has nothing left. {killers} are both in this.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillersNote: End it now and the incident moves to the clean-up. Keep going and the turn order carries on - nobody loses a turn they were owed, and you can end it from the tracker whenever you like.
Murder.crowded: {name} walked in on top of {third}. Four people in one room is not a murder anybody can carry out - the incident is canceled.
Murder.crowdedNote: Nobody dies. What the fight already did stands: the wounds, the Sanity, and anything it left on the floor.
Murder.freeResolution: You stopped them cold. Take Survive or Role Reversal this turn - no roll, it works.
Murder.castMissingHere: This browser holds no cast for the running incident, so its turn cannot be worked out here. Enter the cast by hand (the case's health check), or let the GM whose browser holds it act.
Murder.castNotArrived: The other GMs' copies of the incident's cast have not arrived on this browser yet: try again in a moment.
Murder.deniedByIncident: The incident has taken this one away from you.

Investigation.finalAskBody: You picked a room for the Final Truth Remnant and closed the window without saving. Place it now?
Investigation.plannedRoomGone: The planned room “{room}” is not on this scene. Pick a room.
Investigation.neverOnePerson: A Remnant names nobody: a Key Remnant narrows the suspects to at most half the cast, any other to 2-4.

plannerIntro.one: {n} clue for chapter {chapter}. It should narrow the suspects to {min}-{max} people.
plannerIntro.other: {n} clues for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}-{max} people.

Investigation.placedMeanwhile: Another GM placed this row's Key Remnant while the window was open, so nothing more was placed.
Investigation.tokenGone: Its Remnant is gone from the map
Investigation.keyRetyped: Its Remnant is no longer a Key Remnant

keyOffPlan.one: One found Key Remnant is not on the plan ({names}); it still counts toward the threshold of {bar}.
keyOffPlan.other: {n} found Key Remnants are not on the plan ({names}); they still count toward the threshold of {bar}.

Investigation.deleteTraceAsk: Delete the Remnant “{name}”? Its token is removed from the map and its row from the case.

tooThin.one: Only {found} Key Remnant has been found, and the trial needs more than {min} to have an honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand: each Monokuma's pool gains Despair when the Class Trial opens.
tooThin.other: Only {found} Key Remnants have been found, and the trial needs more than {min} to have an honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand: each Monokuma's pool gains Despair when the Class Trial opens.

Investigation.tooThinNone: No Key Remnant has been found yet, and the trial needs more than {min} to have an honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand: each Monokuma's pool gains Despair when the Class Trial opens.
Investigation.breakdownTooltip: What each Truth Bullet is by the GMs' answer key, whatever its holder was shown.
Investigation.newTraceIntro: The Remnant lands at a random spot in the room; move its token if the spot matters.
Investigation.newTraceTied: Part of this murder (survives the chapter-end sweep)
Investigation.newTraceNote: The name and the description are what a student reads when they find it; what analysis reveals waits until they Analyze it. Only GMs read your note.
Investigation.newTraceBadType: That is not a kind of Remnant this module knows.
Investigation.newTraceUnfindable: Observe has no difficulty for that kind of Remnant at that visibility, so nobody can find it. Open New Remnant again with another kind or visibility.
Investigation.noRooms: This scene has no rooms yet, so there is nowhere to put a Remnant. Draw the regions first; Room setup explains how.
Investigation.createNote: Place puts a row's Key Remnant on the map at once, in the room you pick: reinforced, tied to the crime, somewhere inside the room, with the words typed on its row. A row already on the map has no Place button.
Investigation.keyDcNote: A Key Remnant is the easiest thing in a room to notice. How easy depends on its visibility: {list}. The difficulty scale above does not change it. Ordinary evidence in the same band is three to six points harder to notice. The scale is how much a clue gives away.
Investigation.keyLimitLine: {used} of {limit} Key Remnants used this chapter. The minimum is {min}.
Investigation.keyLimitOverride: Place more than the opening roll allows

savedOver.one: One field changed elsewhere while you edited, so it was not saved: {list}. Reopen Investigation to see what it holds, and type yours again if it should stand.
savedOver.other: {n} fields changed elsewhere while you edited, so they were not saved: {list}. Reopen Investigation to see what they hold, and type yours again if they should stand.

Investigation.saveStopped: The Save stopped part-way: {error}. What it wrote before that stands, and Investigation is open again with it. Type the rest again.

createHereIntro.one: A player named a point of interest, and you decided something is there. This puts a Key Remnant on the map and can attach it to the {n} clue you planned, if it is not on the map yet.
createHereIntro.other: A player named a point of interest, and you decided something is there. This puts a Key Remnant on the map and can attach it to one of the {n} clues you planned that is not on the map yet.

unfoundKeys.one: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants, one short. Each Monokuma's pool gains {despair} Despair: {who}.
unfoundKeys.other: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants, {n} short. Each Monokuma's pool gains {despair} Despair: {who}.

Investigation.keyPublicNote: “Name” and “Player description” are what a finder holds the moment they pick it up; “What analysis reveals” waits until they Analyze it. The Remnants tab edits the same three fields. Only GMs read your note.

leftoverKeys.one: {n} Key Remnant from an earlier chapter is still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see it; clear it at the end of a chapter or attach it here.
leftoverKeys.other: {n} Key Remnants from an earlier chapter are still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see them; clear them at the end of a chapter or attach them here.

Investigation.chargeTooLate: No Despair was charged for unfound Key Remnants: the clock is in chapter {now}, but the last case belongs to chapter {was}, so this chapter has no case to count.

Vault.handsFull: Your hands are full and you have no stash of your own to put it in, so it stays where it was. You can try again this time of day.
Vault.stowTooltip: Put this in your stash (you must be in the room)
Vault.takeTooltip: Take this back out (you must be in the room)
Vault.notHere: Your stash is in {room}. Go there to reach it.
Vault.noStashOnScene: You have no stash on this scene.
Vault.handFirst: “{item}” is broken, so you cannot hold it ready, and you can keep only one piece of {group} stowed. Hold a working one ready first.
Vault.noBullets: Truth Bullets are what you know, so they cannot go in a stash.
Vault.full: Your stash in {room} is full: it holds {limit} things. Take something out before you put something in.
Vault.overflowed: You cannot carry any more {category}, so “{item}” went into your stash.
Vault.rifledAgain: You have already been through {who}'s stash this time of day. Try it again at the next time of day.
Vault.noticed: Something has been moved in your stash, and something is missing from it. You have no idea whose hands have been in it, or when.
Vault.gmPending: {thief} took something from the stash of {owner} in {room} while {owner} was elsewhere. The next time {owner} enters that room, they learn somebody has been in the stash, but not who or when.
Vault.gmWatched: {thief} took something from the stash of {owner} in {room} while {owner} stood there. {owner} saw it, so no notice is left for later.
Vault.gmTold: {owner} entered {room} and was told somebody has been in their stash. It covers what {names} took.
Vault.stashesIntro: Who has a stash in which room. Click a cell to change it. A bedroom's owner has a stash there from the start; you can take it away here.
Vault.stashesNote: Anyone in the room can go through an open stash and take one thing from it, once each time of day. A hidden one must be found first, with Analyze's Find Stash (16+), and is open to its finder from then on. A stash in somebody else's room does not come with a key to it.
Vault.stashCycle: Click to cycle: none / open / hidden

stashNotEmpty.one: {name} has one thing in the stash in {room}. Take it out before you remove the stash.
stashNotEmpty.other: {name} has {n} things in the stash in {room}. Take them out before you remove the stash.

Vault.noOpenStashHere: There is no open stash in this room.
Vault.stashEmpty: Nothing to take: the stash of {who} is empty.
Vault.openStashNote: You can take one thing from each stash listed here, once each time of day.

Vault.keyGave: {who} now has a copy of your key to {room}.

Vault.noKeysToTake: {actor} holds no key to anybody else's room.

Vault.isRoomHint: Whether this region is a room. A region with a Teleport or level-change behavior, or one a player drew, cannot be one.
Vault.notSharedHint: Leave this region out of the rooms-per-student count. It changes no rule.

Vault.neighboursNote: “Neighbours” is where a door overrules the map: list the rooms this one opens into, separated by commas. Two rooms are connected when either lists the other, both ways. A room with a list is connected to nothing else, and a room beside it cannot walk in unless one of the two lists the other. Left blank, a room's neighbours are the rooms without a list whose walls share an edge with its own (a corner is not enough), and every room that lists it. A room the lists and the walls leave with no neighbour has no door out. A room that has no list, is in no list and touches no other room, not even at a corner, is not checked: a crossing from it may go to any room.
Vault.neighboursUnknown: {room}: no room on this scene is named {names}. What was typed stays in its Neighbors and connects nothing until such a room exists.

Vault.imageBroken: This picture does not load - pick the file again.

Chapter.keepBullets: Keep their Truth Bullets (not a killing-game death)
Chapter.deathNote: Their Truth Bullets are destroyed, carried and stashed alike, and that cannot be undone. Everything else stays on the body to be found, and the dead move none of it. The dead stop counting as being in the room: no witnessing, no handovers, no murder blocked.
Chapter.vaultPending: A stash is still their own sheet, so stashed bullets are in the count above and everything else they put away stays there to be found.
Chapter.stageSixTitle: That was the victim of the incident
Chapter.stageSixIntro: {victim} is the victim of the incident {killer} is in, and the incident is still running.
Chapter.stageSixWhat: Moving it to Stage 6 lets {killer} see the Remnants they left and spend Sanity trying to erase them. The incident stays open until you close it, so nothing is announced yet.
Chapter.revived: {name} is no longer marked dead. The Truth Bullets that died with them do not come back.
Chapter.deadPanelNote: The dead take no actions and spend no Hope. Brought back as a Monocub, this panel holds Confusion and the Monocub's other tiles.
Chapter.deadCannotAct: {name} is dead and cannot take actions.
Chapter.keepSecretUntilFound: Keep it the GMs' until the body is found: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets stay until then
Chapter.keptUntilFound: Kept by the GMs until the body is found or you make it known in the Players window. The table sees nothing yet: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets are still on the sheet.
Chapter.nobodyFoundYou: Nobody has found your body yet.
Chapter.youFoundBody: In {room} you find the body of {name}. Nobody else has seen it yet, and nothing is announced.
Chapter.youFoundBodyWith: In {room} you find the body of {name}. You are not the only one here, and nothing is announced until the GM says so.
Chapter.pendingBody: {names} found the body of {name} in {room}. Announce the discovery now?
Chapter.pendingNote: Announce brings everyone to the room and plays the discovery sound to the whole table. Not yet keeps it waiting: you can announce it later with Body found in the Investigation window.

deathsStillSecret.one: {n} death nobody has found is still the GMs' alone. Until you make it known in the Players window, this trial treats that student as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killer, who counts as a Blackened only for a death the table knows.
deathsStillSecret.other: {n} deaths nobody has found are still the GMs' alone. Until you make them known in the Players window, this trial treats those students as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killers, who count as Blackened only for a death the table knows.

Chapter.bodyAnnouncedAlready: {name}'s body was already announced in this chapter, so nothing was announced again. To announce another body in that room, leave the body unnamed.
Chapter.bodyPrimaryOnly: Only the primary GM, {name}, can announce a body. Ask {name}, or announce it when you are the only GM connected.
Chapter.bodyNotPublished: {name}'s death could not be made known to the table, so the discovery does not name them and the death is still the GMs' alone. Make it known in the Players window.
Chapter.noRooms: This scene has no room regions to gather anyone into.
Chapter.bodyNote: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change until you start the Investigation.
Chapter.bodyNoteLater: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change.
Chapter.bodyNoteTraces: Then you are asked which Remnants left while somebody gathered tools belong to this murder.
Chapter.bodyFound: A body has been found in {room}.
Chapter.bodyCalled: Everyone is gathered in the room with the body. The GM will start the Investigation.

promoted.one: {n} Remnant now counts as evidence of this murder.
promoted.other: {n} Remnants now count as evidence of this murder.

Chapter.endIntro: Chapter {chapter} is wrapping up. Tick what should happen.
Chapter.optReveal: Reveal what the Truth Bullets really are, with their readings ({n} to reveal)
Chapter.revealKeeps: Faint Truth Bullets stay hidden, but every Final, Faint or not, shows its kind; both stay, still to be analysed.

Chapter.moved: The clock now reads chapter {chapter}, session {session}.

typeless.other: {n} Truth Bullets not analysed have no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch them - held by {who}. Take them, and give ones with their types from Give / take items.

Chapter.optSweep: Collect the Truth Bullets ({n} would go, Faint and Final stay)
Chapter.optFaint: Clear the Faint Remnants ({n} would go)

doneKeys.one: Took {n} Key Remnant off the map.
doneKeys.other: Took {n} Key Remnants off the map.

Chapter.doneNextMorning: The next chapter opens on the morning of day {day}, with actions and Search Tokens refilled.
Chapter.doneInvestigationOver: The Investigation is over; the campaign is back in Daily Life.

Chapter.notStopped: No end of the chapter waits to be finished.
Chapter.finishPhaseMoved: The end of the chapter stopped in {opened}, and the clock reads {now}. Back in {opened}, Finish the chapter's end does the rest; Drop the rest leaves it undone.

Eclipse.callsLocked: Every Call is locked until the Eclipse ends, whatever Hope or Despair you hold.
Eclipse.murderWindowLocked: No incident opens during an Eclipse. Open it once the Eclipse ends; a trap's card keeps its button until then.
Eclipse.murderLocked: No incident opens during an Eclipse. A Direct Murder declared in it is judged when the Eclipse ends.
Eclipse.bodyLocked: You cannot announce a body during an Eclipse, and no body is discovered automatically either. Wait until the Eclipse ends.

Movement.unlawfulArrival: {name} reached {room} by a crossing the rules do not allow, and was not put back. Until they stand in a room they could reach from {from}, they do not count as a witness to a body or a third party to a murder. Moving the token as a GM makes their spot lawful.
Movement.wallCrossed: {name}'s token was moved through a wall on {scene} and was sent back where it stood.
Movement.floorJumped: {name}'s token was moved to another floor on {scene} where no stairs lead, and was sent back where it stood.
Movement.ruleSentBack: {name}'s token was moved into {room} on {scene}, where the rules do not let {name} go, and was put back where {name} last stood.
Movement.dropRemoved: A player placed a token of {name} in {room} on {scene}, where the rules do not let {name} stand. The token was removed.
Movement.droppedFromNowhere: A player placed a token of {name} in {room} on {scene}, where {name} had not stood before. As an arrival from outside the rooms, it was exempt from the connected-rooms rule and counts as a witness there. Move it if it should not be there.

Move.title: Move
Move.drag: To move to another room, drag your token there.
Move.freeAvailable: The next room takes your Free Move, and your actions stay.
Move.freeSpent: Free Move used. The next room costs an action; you have {left}.
Move.nextSprint: Free Move used. The next room takes a free crossing, and your actions stay.
Move.nextBurst: Free Move used. The next room takes your Burst, and your actions stay.
Move.leftRooms: You are no longer in any room.

wasSprint.one: Paid by a free crossing. {n} left.
wasSprint.other: Paid by a free crossing. {n} left.

Move.wasFree: That was your Free Move for this time of day.

costAction.one: That cost an action. You have {left} action left.
costAction.other: That cost an action. You have {left} actions left.

Move.noBudget: No Free Move and no actions left.
Move.notConnected: {to} is not connected to {from}. From here you can reach: {rooms}
Move.noBudgetLong: You have no Free Move and no actions left, so your token was put back.
Move.refundedBack: The GM gave back your last crossing, and your token is back where it was.
Move.refundedStays: The GM gave back your last crossing, but your token could not be moved back. Ask the GM.
Move.refundedPrice: What the crossing cost is yours again.
Move.refundedNoPrice: No price came back for that crossing. If you paid for it, ask the GM.
Move.noStairs: No stairs lead from {from} to that floor.
Move.dead: They are dead. The body stays where it fell.

Project.passageRefused: That stretch does not stand between the builder's room and the room beyond: pick it again.
Project.passageNoWall: The builder's room shares no wall with another room on this floor: a secret passage has nowhere to go.
Project.passageNeedsPick: Pick the stretch of wall the secret passage goes through first.
Project.passagePick: Pick the stretch on the wall
Project.passageFrom: From the {room}, where the builder stands.
Project.passageNote: A secret passage through a wall of the room you are in: Hand, Complex (6), always secret. Only you, and whoever the project is shared with before it is finished, will know it.
Project.breachNote: A breach through a wall of the room you are in: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the hole is there for everyone to see.
Project.sealNote: Seal the passage: Hand, Complex (6). Once it is finished the passage is closed, for you and for everyone who knows it; a GM can open it again.
Project.unbreachNote: Close the breach: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the wall stands whole again.
Project.repairNote: Repair an item: Hand; Trivial (3) for an item of Tier 0 or 1, Complex (6) for Tier 2 or 3. Once it is finished the item is whole again.
Project.repairLockNote: Repair the Lock: Hand, Trivial (3). Once it is finished the lock holds again, for everyone.
Project.notRepaired: {name} is finished, but its item could not be repaired: {why}
Project.needsKiller: An indirect murder needs a killer: pick who it is visible to, or approve it from the proposal card.
Project.needsKillerNamed: “{name}” cannot become an indirect murder from here - open it and name who the trap belongs to.
Project.title: Project
Project.choosePrompt: Start something new, or push a project that already exists?
Project.agreedWarning: Fill this in as your side of the agreement. The GM reads it, may change the scale, the room, or the wording, and only then does the project exist.
Project.startNote: Nothing is created yet. This goes to the GM as a proposal - they approve it, adjust it, or turn it down.
Project.indirectMine: Indirect murder - kept secret, so only you and the GMs see it
Project.traitRequired: A project needs a statistic: pick the one its work demands.
Project.repaired: repaired. {name} can be worked on again.
Project.doneBody: {name} is complete - all {target} progress is in. Ask the GM what it does for you now.
Project.frozenNow: {name} is broken and frozen until {repair} is finished.
Project.alreadyFrozen: {name} is already broken and waiting on a repair.
Project.sabotageNotApplied: The roll succeeded, but no GM confirmed the damage in time. Tell your GM: {name} may not be broken.
Project.none: No projects yet. Start one first.
Project.noneToMove: No project here has progress that can move. Finished ones are done, and a sabotaged one waits for its repair.
Project.aloneBonus: Nobody else is in the room, so the project gains +1 progress.
Project.concealSeen: {actor} is busy with something in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.
Project.tracesUncovered: not rolled: the Remnants stay as they were left.
Project.toolRelief: “{item}” is Tier {tier}, so every threshold on this roll comes down by {tier}.
Project.roomOnNoScene: No project was made: {room} is a room on no scene now. Name a room a scene holds, or none.
Project.seenUnknown: Progress unknown: it shows when one of your characters is in this project's room.
Project.seenAsLast: Progress as one of your characters last saw it in this project's room.
Project.cardFrozen: Broken, and frozen until it is repaired
Project.cardSecret: Secret - only the people ticked on it
Project.cardPublic: Public - anyone who has stood in its room
Project.cardShared: Every project token is a copy of this actor. Open a project from its token on the map.
Project.cardUnknown: You do not know what this is.
Project.createNote: Only Work on Project adds progress.
Project.name: Name
Project.visibleToNote: Whoever builds it always sees it.
Project.manageIntro: A project can belong to a room. Only characters standing there can work on it or sabotage it.
Project.secretNote: Indirect murder projects are secret by default: only the killer and the GMs see them. Share to bring in a co-conspirator.
Project.changeImage: Click to change this project's image
Project.tokenMoved: {project} now belongs to {to} - its token was moved there from {from}.

sweptOld.one: {n} project token was left on the map by a project that no longer exists, and has been removed.
sweptOld.other: {n} project tokens were left on the map by projects that no longer exist, and have been removed.

duplicates.one: A project stands on the map twice: {list}. The token the project points at is kept and the spare one is left where it is - delete it by hand if it is a mistake.
duplicates.other: {n} spare project tokens stand beside the ones their projects point at: {list}. Nothing was removed - delete them by hand if they are mistakes.

Project.glyphNote: Under the Stained Glass theme the Projects tray draws this instead of the image, in the interface's color. The image is used everywhere else.
Project.deleteNote: Delete in a project's row asks first, then removes the project for good. Its progress and metadata do not come back.
Project.shareIntro: Let another player see this project. Players can bring in a co-conspirator; GMs can share with anyone.
Project.noPlayers: There are no players to share with.
Project.alreadyFull: {name} is already at {current}/{target}. No progress left to add.
Project.alreadyEmpty: {name} is already at 0. Nothing left to take away.
Project.noneHere: There is no project started in {room}.
Project.allSabotaged: Everything here is already broken or is itself a repair: {names}.
Project.someSabotaged: Not offered - already broken, or a repair project: {names}.
Project.editProgressNote: Progress is kept: this project is at {current}/{target}. Lowering the scale below what is earned clamps it.
Project.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}”? Its progress goes with it.
Project.conditionPlaceholder: whoever opens the dumbwaiter after dark
Project.conditionNote: Indirect murder only. Name a condition instead of a victim - whoever meets it is who the trap catches.
Project.trapNoCondition: No condition was written down for this trap. Agree one before firing it.
Project.proposalPrompt: Say what you are actually doing and why here. The GM reads this with your answers and decides - they may change the scale, the room or the wording before it starts.
Project.proposalPlaceholder: What you are building, and what you want out of it…
Project.proposerKnows: Your project “{name}” is under way in {room}. It shows on your Projects tray and on the map.
Project.facilityTold: Your project {name} gives a room action: {action}.
Project.sightTold: You are in on the secret project {name}.
Project.sightGone: You are no longer in on a secret project.
Project.facilityGone: Your project {name} no longer gives a room action.
Project.proposalSent: “{name}” has gone to the GM. Nothing starts until they approve it.
Project.proposalNotSent: Nothing was sent to the GM.
Project.declinedPlayer: {name} turned down that project. Talk to them about what would work instead.

workOnHint.one: Push the {n} project running in this room.
workOnHint.other: Push one of the {n} projects running in this room.

Project.startNewHint: Describe something new. Nothing exists until the GM approves it.

sabotageHint.one: Break this room's one breakable project so it needs a repair; you always leave a Remnant.
sabotageHint.other: Break one of this room's {n} projects so it needs a repair; you always leave a Remnant.

Project.alreadyComplete: {name} is finished. There is no work left in it.
Project.allComplete: Every project in {room} is already finished.
Project.frozenNoProgress: {name} has been sabotaged and cannot move forward until its repair is finished.
Project.effectFailed: {name}: part of what finishing it (or taking it back under its target) does could not be done ({error}). The bar stands as it is; the console has the details.
Project.everyone: Public: everyone can see it. Ticked: who knew before it was revealed - they and whoever builds it are who will know if it is sealed again.
Project.builderStays: {name} is building “{project}”: a builder cannot be taken off their own project.
Project.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. A false back in the bookcase, deep enough to hide a notebook
Project.descriptionNote: Everyone who knows the project sees it. At most {max} characters.
Project.descriptionTooLong: A description holds at most {max} characters, and this one has {n}. Shorten it.
Project.trayLessTooltip: Take one point of progress off this project
Project.trayMoreTooltip: Add one point of progress to this project

TraitRuling.title: Which statistic?
TraitRuling.gmBody: The roll lists several statistics. Pick one from what the player says their character does.
TraitRuling.waiting: The GM is choosing the statistic. Tell them in your thread what you do.
TraitRuling.refused: The GM turned the action down, so you keep it.
TraitRuling.openingKiller: The GM is choosing the statistic for your opening. Tell them in your thread how you go about it.
TraitRuling.openingKillerProposed: The GM is ruling on the statistic you proposed for your opening.
TraitRuling.openingVictim: The GM is setting up a roll for you.
TraitRuling.gmBodyProposed: The player proposes a statistic. Approve it, change it to another on the list, or refuse.
TraitRuling.changedBody: You proposed {proposed}. The GM changed it to {stat}. Nothing has been spent yet.
TraitRuling.passedLine: I'll pass on the roll ({stat}). Nothing was spent.
TraitRuling.projectBody: This project was stored without a statistic. Propose one: the GM approves or changes it, and it stays the project's.

DiceLook.setByGm: Your dice look is set by the GM.
DiceLook.settingBack: {name} changed the table's dice look settings, which only a full Gamemaster may change, so they were put back.
DiceLook.settingBackUnheard: The table's dice look settings were changed with no trace of who changed them, and only a full Gamemaster may change them, so they were put back.
DiceLook.stopped: {name}'s dice look keeps changing straight back, so it is left as it is for a minute, then put back at its next change or throw.

diag.title: Dice look
diag.introGm: The dice look as seen here. A player's own look only they can check.
diag.introPlayer: What this browser reads of your dice look. Copy the text at the foot of the window and send it to your GM.
diag.findings: Why the dice may look different

forced.off: not forced: the setting is off

diag.preset: Daggerheart's Hope and Despair dice on this browser
diag.presetNone: none (Daggerheart 2.10 and later color them by Dice So Nice roles)
diag.tableLook: The table's Hope and Despair look, laid on each throw here
diag.lastWindow: Last roll window on this browser
diag.nothingFound: Nothing found that makes this browser draw the dice differently.

finding.notForced: {name} does not hold the table's dice look yet. The primary GM puts it back at their next change or throw.
finding.fuseStopped: {name}'s dice look kept changing back, so it is left as it is for a minute.
finding.overlay: A character of {name}'s carries a dice look of its own: {actors}.
finding.onlyMine: {name} has Dice So Nice's "only my dice" on, so nobody else's dice are drawn on their screen.
finding.othersSfxOff: {name} has other players' special effects switched off.
finding.lowQuality: {name} draws dice at low image quality.
finding.presetDiffers: {duality} of the roll read carries another preset than this browser's Daggerheart setting: it was thrown on another browser.
finding.presetMissing: {duality} of the roll read carries no Daggerheart preset, so it is drawn in its thrower's Dice So Nice look.
finding.presetMissingLaid: {duality} of the roll read carries no Daggerheart preset of its own; with one look for the table, this browser draws it in the table's Hope and Despair look.
finding.presetDiffersLaid: {duality} of the roll read carries another preset than the table's Hope and Despair look; with one look for the table, this browser draws it in the table's look over its own.
finding.missingSystem: Dice So Nice on this browser has no dice system "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn as standard dice here.
finding.missingColorset: Dice So Nice on this browser has no colorset "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn in a custom color here.
finding.missingTexture: Dice So Nice on this browser has no texture "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn with no texture here.
finding.missingMaterial: Dice So Nice on this browser has no material "{name}", so dice that use it are drawn in the automatic material here.
finding.dsnApiMoved: Dice So Nice {version} copies only part of the GM's look; players fill in the rest their own way.
finding.rolesUnforced: Daggerheart {version} colors its Hope and Despair dice by Dice So Nice roles, which the table's forced look does not set.
finding.otherBrowser: {name}'s browser is not read here. Ask them to run game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook() and send you its text.

RollDialog.locked: You cannot change this here. Advantage and disadvantage come from Calls, the situation, a hindrance die, or Breakdown. An experience comes only from the Talent Call, which a GM approves.
RollDialog.advantageLocked: Advantage and disadvantage come from Calls, the situation, a hindrance die, or Breakdown; you cannot set them in this window.
RollDialog.pickOneExperience: Pick the one experience this roll relates to. Clicking another moves the choice.
RollDialog.experienceLocked: An experience counts on a roll only through the Talent Hope Call, which a GM approves.
RollDialog.bonusLocked: You cannot add a bonus here. A bonus comes from a Call or an effect on your character.
RollDialog.modeLocked: The game sets who sees this roll; you cannot change it in this window.
RollDialog.modeRoom: The GMs, you, and everyone in your room
RollDialog.actionLocked: This roll's Hope or Despair decides what happens next, so it is an action, never a reaction.
RollDialog.reactionLocked: A statistic rolled on its own is a reaction: it costs nothing and earns nothing. Hope and Despair come from actions.
RollDialog.unlockedByCall: Unlocked by a Call you paid for.
RollDialog.freeCritArmed: Loaded Die is armed: a random die is set to 12, and you roll the other. It is a critical only if the rolled die also comes up 12; otherwise the roll is with Hope if the Hope die was set, with Despair if not.
RollDialog.forcedByCall: Set by a Call. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.forcedByHindrance: A hindrance die is on this roll. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.forcedBySituation: Set by your situation, such as the room, the time of day, or a tool in hand. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.forcedByState: You are in Breakdown: every roll is at disadvantage until you have some Sanity again. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.lockedByCall: This roll's advantage or disadvantage is already set.
RollDialog.stackedAdvantage: Advantage ×{n} from {sources}. You roll {n} advantage dice and the best one counts. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.stackedDisadvantage: Disadvantage ×{n} from {sources}. You roll {n} disadvantage dice and the worst one counts. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.mixedAdvantage: Advantage, after {sources} partly cancel out. You cannot turn it off.
RollDialog.mixedDisadvantage: Disadvantage, after {sources} partly cancel out. You cannot turn it off.

advantageCapped.one: A roll takes no more than {cap} of these dice.
advantageCapped.other: A roll takes no more than {cap} of these dice.

what.despair.roster: Granting, revoking, or naming a Despair pool
