Bridge.nothingSpent: You keep your action and your Hope.
Bridge.emptyRequest: Nothing was sent - write your request first.

why.unknownSender: The GM does not see you as connected. Reload and try again.
why.notYours: It names a character you do not play.
why.gmOnly: Only a GM can ask for that.
why.missing: What it names is not there any more.
why.badRequest: The GM's side could not read that request.
why.outOfRange: A number in it is out of range.
why.busy: It is already being written. Wait a moment and look again.
why.notOffered: No Level Up is on offer for that character.
why.notSecret: Only a secret project can be shared.
why.notAPlayer: A project can only be shared with a player.
why.notHolding: None of your characters in the fight holds that object.
why.alreadyHeld: That character already holds that Call.
why.notASupport: That Call cannot be bought for that character.
why.hopeBarred: You cannot spend a Hope Call right now.
why.notEnoughHope: The character paying does not hold enough Hope.
why.noReroll: Only a Reroll of that character's roll from the last few minutes can take it back.
why.undoIsTheGms: Taking a result back is the GM's: a Reroll is asked of the GM, who takes the first result back.
why.traceOutOfReach: A Reroll can no longer reach that Remnant.
why.notInIncident: Your character is not in a running incident.
why.actionLocked: That action is locked for now.
why.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
why.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
why.actionDenied: That action is not open to that character now.
why.nothingLeft: There is nothing left to spend.
why.movedOn: The incident has moved on since that action.
why.notThatRepair: That is not the repair your sabotage made.
why.notWhereItStood: The token did not stand there a moment ago.
why.nothingToUndo: There is nothing of that to take back.
why.deathStands: That crisis action killed somebody: the death stands, and it cannot be taken back.
why.notThere: The character is not where it needs to be.
why.relay: This game leaves that change to the GM.
why.failed: It failed on the GM's side; the GM can see the details.
why.noAnswer: The GM's client did not answer in time.
why.capReached: That student has had a Monocub's move this time of day. You keep your action and Hope.
why.capDay: That student has had two Monocub moves today. You keep your action and Hope.
why.answerKeyMissing: The GM's browser does not hold this bullet's answer key. The GM has been told.
why.keysNotOpen: The GM's browser has not opened the answer keys yet. The GM has been told.
why.rollUnknown: The GM's client holds no roll of yours that it could be scored on.
why.rollNotYours: The roll it names is not your character's.
why.rollOtherAction: The roll it names was thrown for another action.
why.rollUsed: That roll has already been scored.
why.rollStale: The roll it names is too old to be scored.
why.rollMissed: The roll it names did not earn that.
why.projectFrozen: That project is frozen by a sabotage until its repair is finished.
why.rollReplaced: A later roll of the same action replaced the roll it names.
why.notPaid: No action was paid for that roll. Take the action again.
why.rollThrown: That action's roll has been thrown already.
why.callNotPaid: No Hope was paid for that Call.
why.callNotApproved: That Call has no yes from a GM. Ask for it again.
why.itemNotDecided: No GM has decided yet on that item, which a player made on a sheet: it changes no hands until one does.
why.notEligible: You hold no ballot in this vote.
why.wrongCount: Your ballot does not name as many people as the vote asks for.
why.sheetPutBack: That change to your sheet was undone: no action in the game accounts for it.
why.notKnown: You do not know that secret passage.
why.recipientDead: The one you chose is dead. Nothing was shown.
why.floorClosed: The debate is not open to an Objection now.
why.noSpeaker: Nobody has spoken in this trial yet, so there is nobody to object to.
why.noBullet: You hold no Truth Bullet to prove an Objection with.
why.objectionOver: That Objection is no longer waiting for a Truth Bullet.
why.notAtPassage: Stand on the passage's mark, or a square next to it, first.
why.oneWay: This passage cannot be taken from this side.
why.roomSealed: That room is sealed for this time of day. Nobody gets in.
why.onWatch: You keep watch: you stay at your post until the Eclipse ends.
why.chained: You are chained here until this time of day ends.
why.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action - Survive, Escape Together, a Finishing Blow, or, if you only walked in on it, Averted Eyes.
why.trialLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Nobody leaves the courtroom until it ends.
why.noBudget: No Free Move and no actions left.
why.eclipseSpent: Your Eclipse crossings are used up.
why.roundMovedOn: The GM is asking again: answer the new question.
why.notInRound: This question is for the players whose students are in play, and yours is not.

Bridge.criticalHint: Critical - this player is owed a substantial hint.
Bridge.declined: {name} turned the attempt down. Your action is back.
Bridge.declinedGm: Turned down. {name} has the action back.
Bridge.settledExpired: Nobody answered in time - ask again.
Bridge.settledGone: The player was no longer waiting.
Bridge.settledUnconfirmed: Answered by {name} - not confirmed as received.
Bridge.claimBusy: {gm} is ruling on this card right now.
Bridge.alreadySettled: This card has already been answered.

Tables.installed: Item tables ready: {created} created, {skipped} already existed.

allPresent.one: {n} item table already exists in this world.
allPresent.other: All {n} item tables already exist in this world.

Tables.rebuildNote: Rebuilding deletes the default item tables and builds them again from the module's own lists. Anything you edited by hand is lost.

someFailed.one: {n} item table could not be created. See the console.
someFailed.other: {n} item tables could not be created. See the console.

Tables.whereNote: A Search draws from the room's tables first, then from the tier pools.
Tables.noRoomPools: No room pools yet. Name one below.
Tables.newTierPoolNote: A tier pool's name gives its category and tier, such as “DRPG Tools - Tier 2”. You rarely need to make one by hand: “Install / reinstall” below builds them all.
Tables.newTierPoolForms: “{name}” is not a tier pool's name. Use one of these, where N is a tier from {low} to {high}: {forms}.
Tables.renameOtherPool: “{name}” would name another pool. This one holds the items of “{pool}”: keep its category and tier in the name.
Tables.installTabNote: “Install / reinstall” below builds the default set, one table per category and tier. If they already exist, you choose between keeping yours and rebuilding.
Tables.editorIntro: Everything a Search can turn up. Pick a table on the left.
Tables.roomBreakdown: Grouped by the category the tier pools give each name. A room table with no category in its name can supply any category a Search asks for. Name a table after the room's table and a category, as “Kitchen - Murder Weapons”, and the names no pool holds count as that category.
Tables.unfiledNote: No tier pool holds these names, so the module cannot tell what they are or how good they are. In a room table with no category in its name, they can come up for any category. Use the arrows on a row to put one in a tier pool.
Tables.placeTooltip: Choose the pools that hold this item
Tables.placeIntro: Tick every pool this item should be in. Ticking a new pool copies it there, and unticking one takes it out. To move it, untick the pool you are viewing and tick another.
Tables.placeRolesNote: The description, the picture, and the roles travel with it. A tier pool below Tier 2 takes no roles, and an item cannot take its pool's own category as a role.
Tables.placeNone: An item has to live in at least one pool. Use the row's ✕ to delete it outright.
Tables.placeUnchanged: “{name}” is already in exactly those pools.
Tables.tierTargetIs: Goes into {table}. Worked out from the category and tier above.

GiveBack.title: Give back Foundry's settings
GiveBack.intro: While it runs, this module changes these settings of Foundry, Daggerheart, and the modules it needs:

what.automation: Daggerheart's Vulnerable and Defeated automations are off: Breakdown and Wounded take their place.
what.playerFiles: Players and Trusted Players cannot browse or upload files ('Keep players out of the file browser').
what.isoWelcome: Isometric Perspective's welcome window stays closed for everyone.
what.dhWelcome: Daggerheart's welcome journal does not open for anyone.
what.liveKitInFoundry: LiveKit's voice stays inside the Foundry window for everyone.
what.rtcDock: Foundry's camera dock is folded while the voice tile is on, and no camera pops out.
what.sceneVision: On scenes with rooms, the rooms take over Foundry's own vision, fog, and global light: turning 'Rooms decide what players can see' off gives them back.
what.diceLook: With one look for the table in 'Dice look for the table', every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice in one full Gamemaster's look. Give back does not change this, and nobody's own earlier look comes back: the module never kept it.

phase.eclipse: The lights are out. Everyone places their token, {reach} or anywhere at night, and nobody sees who went where. Your actions are already refilled, but you can spend them only on a Direct Murder, and nobody makes a Call until the lights come up.
phase.dailyLife: Ordinary days inside the school. You have {actions} each time of day to search rooms, work on projects, rest, talk, and prepare. No body has been found yet this chapter, and this is when you decide who you trust.

phase.classTrial: Everyone is in the room and one of you did it. Testimony, Objections, and finally the vote. Get it right and the killer is punished; get it wrong and everybody else is.

despair.title: What Despair is
despair.what: Despair is the currency of the Monokuma side. When a student's roll lands with Despair, it feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma, if the GM has turned this on.
despair.spent: It is spent on Despair Calls, the moves that make life harder for the students. The more of it there is, the more the school can do to you.
despair.masked: Every pool's count is public, and the rows above show how full each one is. Only the Overflow's count is hidden from you.
despair.noPools: No Monokuma has a pool yet.

status.actionsWhat: {actions} each time of day. Searching a room, working on a project, observing a Remnant, and analyzing a Truth Bullet each cost one. A Short Rest costs {short}, a Long Rest {long}.
status.actionsWounded: With no Health left you get {wounded} instead of {actions} in Daily Life and the Investigation, until somebody patches you up. In the Class Trial, Wounded takes no action.
status.actionsNow: You have {left} of {max} actions left this time of day.
status.moveWhat: Each time of day, your first crossing into another room is free. After that, each crossing costs an action, or one of the extra crossings you bought with Sprint.
status.moveSpent: You have used your Free Move this time of day. Your next crossing costs an action, or a crossing you bought with Sprint.
status.hopeWhat: Hope is yours, and you spend it on Hope Calls, such as helping another student's roll, leaning on an Experience, invoking your Ultimate, or taking a Reroll. When your roll lands with Hope, you gain more.
status.monokumaActions: You have no actions: none are refilled for you, and nothing you do spends one.
status.monokumaMove: Moving costs you nothing, and you have no Free Move to keep track of.
status.monokumaDespair: You spend Despair where a student spends Hope. The pools are at the top of the screen.
status.monokumaWalls: Walls and locked doors do not apply to you.

projects.title: What a project is
projects.what: A project is a job that takes several actions: building, fixing, poisoning, or digging through something. Each one belongs to a room and moves forward only when somebody works on it there or adds to it with the Contribution Call.
projects.progress: Working on a project costs an action and a roll, and the roll decides how much progress it makes. When the bar fills, the project is finished.
projects.secret: Some projects are secret, known only to the people working on them. Your list shows only the projects you know of.
projects.none: You don't know of any project yet.

defaultName.problem: Room still has the name Foundry gave it
defaultName.why: A room is its name: players read it on the map, and keys, stashes, and Room setup all name it. Give it the room's own name before play.

piecesDiffer.problem: Pieces of this room are set up differently
piecesDiffer.why: A room drawn in several pieces reads each setting from the first piece that has it, so another piece's setting is not the room's. In Room setup change the room's setting, Apply, then set it back and Apply: that gives every piece the same. Set the height in each piece's region settings.

noShape.problem: No geometry the fog can read
noShape.why: The region exists but its shape came back empty: nothing about this room will be drawn.

overlap.title: Rooms overlap
overlap.fact: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms.
overlap.deep: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms, reaching {depth} squares in.
overlap.why: Where two rooms overlap, one room's border runs across the other's floor with no wall near it, and the whole shared border reads as one doorway. Rooms should touch; a sliver thinner than a quarter square is ignored.

adrift.problem: Border runs away from the walls
adrift.fact: {squares} squares of border with no wall.
adrift.why: A border drawn away from the wall it stands for turns that whole side of the room into a doorway: the wall is never found, so nothing closes it.

sealed.title: No way out: walled in
sealed.fact: Every stretch of the border is walled.
sealed.why: Nothing glows as a doorway. If the room should have a way out, add the missing door.

isolated.title: No way out: no neighbor
isolated.fact: No room within a square of the border.
isolated.why: The next room is more than a square away, so the two never meet at a doorway. Rooms should touch along the edge they share.

lattice.why: The rest of the map is drawn to a half-square grid. Draw with snapping on: a corner a fraction of a square out is too small to see, yet it can make two rooms overlap or miss.
